blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: Spiral model — Iterative methodology driven by risk identification and evaluation.
risk analysis — Evaluate probability/impact of potential problems.
RAD — Rapid Application Development using frequent prototypes and feedback.
prototype — Early working or mock representation for evaluation.
stakeholder — Person or group affected by or using the system.

blocks.title: Spiral focuses on risk
blocks.text: Each cycle plans objectives, identifies or resolves major risks, develops/tests and reviews with stakeholders.

blocks.title: RAD is prototype-led
blocks.text: Users evaluate quickly produced models. Frequent prototyping accelerates understanding and can reveal unclear requirements.

blocks.title: Compare suitability
blocks.text: Spiral can suit large/high-risk systems but increases management cost; RAD relies on accessible users and skilled teams and may compromise architecture if rushed.

blocks.title: Worked example · Predict first
blocks.text: Spiral is appropriate because major technical and safety risks need assessment at each cycle.

blocks.title: Worked example · Model and explain
blocks.text: It demands experienced risk assessment and carries greater time/management overhead than simpler methods.
